review_reference: The website's contract in health main BACKEND-NEEDS.md section 1 ("Patient-added records, with photos and files"); the coordinator in chat, 4 Nov 2026: files get their own switch, PATIENT_ENTRY_FILES_ENABLED, on by default; the number 0117 assigned by the coordinator. Stacked on 0116 (PR #163), which is signed separately. Unsigned until the owner signs.
evidence: In plain words, applying 0117 to production does this. It adds three new tables and a view for the photos and PDFs patients attach to the records they add themselves (0116), and five new database commands: two the patient's session uses (open an upload link for one file, confirm it) and three the existing virus-scan bridge's account uses through ehr-api's existing scanner routes (find a file by its storage key, list files waiting for a scan, record a scan result). It changes no existing table's data, row-level security or FORCE setting, no existing function and no existing grant; the only change to an existing object is the chat search tables' list of source kinds, which gains patient_entry_document (as 0116 added patient_entry), validated under a lock taken for at most 5 seconds. Files use the staff documents' bucket, key format and upload links, so no Terraform or bridge change. Limits are enforced in the database under 0116's per-patient lock: 5 files a record, 10 a patient per Lagos day (every link opened counts, removed records' included), JPEG, PNG or PDF, 1 byte to 10 MB. A removed record's files are read by nobody and kept. Proven on PostgreSQL 16.15 under a NOSUPERUSER NOBYPASSRLS migrator: the dry run, the apply, the role bootstrap, the new suite patient-entry-documents.integration.sql and every database suite, the lock bounds (55P03 after 5.1 s with nothing applied), and the release rehearsal.
